items.prompt: Write a Python function `add_digits(n)` that returns the sum of the decimal digits of the non-negative integer n. Use only the Python standard library. Respond with the complete function in a single Python code block and no explanation.

Write a Python function `is_prime(n)` that returns True if the integer n is a prime number and False otherwise (numbers below 2 are not prime). Use only the Python standard library. Respond with the complete function in a single Python code block and no explanation.

Write a Python function `reverse_words(s)` that returns the words of s (separated by single spaces) in reverse order, joined by single spaces. Use only the Python standard library. Respond with the complete function in a single Python code block and no explanation.

Write a Python function `count_vowels(s)` that returns how many characters of s are vowels (a, e, i, o, u), case-insensitive. Use only the Python standard library. Respond with the complete function in a single Python code block and no explanation.

Write a Python function `fizzbuzz(n)` that returns a list of strings for 1..n where multiples of 3 are 'Fizz', multiples of 5 are 'Buzz', multiples of both are 'FizzBuzz' and other numbers are their decimal string. Use only the Python standard library. Respond with the complete function in a single Python code block and no explanation.

Write a Python function `factorial(n)` that returns n! for a non-negative integer n (0! is 1). Use only the Python standard library. Respond with the complete function in a single Python code block and no explanation.

Write a Python function `fibonacci(n)` that returns the n-th Fibonacci number where fibonacci(0) == 0 and fibonacci(1) == 1. Use only the Python standard library. Respond with the complete function in a single Python code block and no explanation.

Write a Python function `gcd(a, b)` that returns the greatest common divisor of non-negative integers a and b, with gcd(0, 0) == 0. Use only the Python standard library. Respond with the complete function in a single Python code block and no explanation.

Write a Python function `flatten(nested)` that returns a flat list of all integers in an arbitrarily nested list, in left-to-right order. Use only the Python standard library. Respond with the complete function in a single Python code block and no explanation.

Write a Python function `second_largest(items)` that returns the second largest distinct value in a list of integers, or None if there are fewer than two distinct values. Use only the Python standard library. Respond with the complete function in a single Python code block and no explanation.

Write a Python function `is_anagram(a, b)` that returns True if string b is a rearrangement of exactly the characters of string a (case-sensitive). Use only the Python standard library. Respond with the complete function in a single Python code block and no explanation.

Write a Python function `run_length_encode(s)` that returns a run-length encoding where each run of a repeated character becomes the character followed by the run length, e.g. 'aab' becomes 'a2b1'. Use only the Python standard library. Respond with the complete function in a single Python code block and no explanation.

Write a Python function `chunk(items, size)` that splits the list items into consecutive sublists of length size (the last one may be shorter). Use only the Python standard library. Respond with the complete function in a single Python code block and no explanation.

Write a Python function `rotate_left(items, k)` that returns a new list rotated left by k positions (k may exceed the length; an empty list stays empty). Use only the Python standard library. Respond with the complete function in a single Python code block and no explanation.

Write a Python function `transpose(matrix)` that returns the transpose of a rectangular matrix given as a list of row lists (an empty matrix gives []). Use only the Python standard library. Respond with the complete function in a single Python code block and no explanation.

Write a Python function `merge_sorted(a, b)` that merges two ascending lists of integers into one ascending list. Use only the Python standard library. Respond with the complete function in a single Python code block and no explanation.

Write a Python function `word_counts(text)` that returns a dictionary mapping each lowercase word to how many times it appears; words are separated by whitespace and compared case-insensitively. Use only the Python standard library. Respond with the complete function in a single Python code block and no explanation.

Write a Python function `title_case(s)` that returns s where every space-separated word has its first character uppercased and the rest lowercased. Use only the Python standard library. Respond with the complete function in a single Python code block and no explanation.

Write a Python function `balanced_brackets(s)` that returns True if the brackets (), [] and {} in s are balanced and properly nested; other characters are ignored. Use only the Python standard library. Respond with the complete function in a single Python code block and no explanation.

Write a Python function `binary_to_int(s)` that converts a non-empty string of '0' and '1' characters to the integer it represents in base 2. Use only the Python standard library. Respond with the complete function in a single Python code block and no explanation.

Write a Python function `int_to_roman(n)` that converts an integer from 1 to 3999 to an uppercase Roman numeral using standard subtractive notation. Use only the Python standard library. Respond with the complete function in a single Python code block and no explanation.

Write a Python function `roman_to_int(s)` that converts a valid uppercase Roman numeral (standard subtractive notation) to an integer. Use only the Python standard library. Respond with the complete function in a single Python code block and no explanation.

Write a Python function `longest_common_prefix(words)` that returns the longest string that is a prefix of every string in the list words ('' for an empty list). Use only the Python standard library. Respond with the complete function in a single Python code block and no explanation.

Write a Python function `two_sum(nums, target)` that returns [i, j] with i < j for the first pair (smallest i, then smallest j) whose values sum to target, or [] if none exists. Use only the Python standard library. Respond with the complete function in a single Python code block and no explanation.

Write a Python function `max_subarray_sum(nums)` that returns the largest sum of a non-empty contiguous sublist of the non-empty integer list nums. Use only the Python standard library. Respond with the complete function in a single Python code block and no explanation.

Write a Python function `unique_paths(m, n)` that returns the number of paths from the top-left to the bottom-right cell of a grid with m rows and n columns when each step moves one cell right or one cell down. Use only the Python standard library. Respond with the complete function in a single Python code block and no explanation.

Write a Python function `binary_search(items, target)` that returns the index of target in a sorted list of distinct integers, or -1 if absent. Use only the Python standard library. Respond with the complete function in a single Python code block and no explanation.

Write a Python function `is_palindrome(text)` that returns whether text equals its reverse (case-sensitive). Use only the Python standard library. Respond with the complete function in a single Python code block and no explanation.

Write a Python function `deduplicate(items)` that returns a list with duplicates removed, preserving the order of first occurrence. Use only the Python standard library. Respond with the complete function in a single Python code block and no explanation.

Write a Python function `caesar_shift(text, k)` that shifts each lowercase letter a-z forward by k positions in the alphabet, wrapping around; all other characters are unchanged. Use only the Python standard library. Respond with the complete function in a single Python code block and no explanation.

Write a Python function `pascal_row(n)` that returns row n (0-indexed) of Pascal's triangle as a list of integers. Use only the Python standard library. Respond with the complete function in a single Python code block and no explanation.

Write a Python function `sum_of_multiples(limit)` that returns the sum of all non-negative integers below limit that are divisible by 3 or 5. Use only the Python standard library. Respond with the complete function in a single Python code block and no explanation.

Write a Python function `mode(items)` that returns the most frequent value in a non-empty list of integers; if several values tie, return the smallest of them. Use only the Python standard library. Respond with the complete function in a single Python code block and no explanation.

Write a Python function `median(items)` that returns the median of a non-empty list of integers as a float (the mean of the two middle values for even lengths). Use only the Python standard library. Respond with the complete function in a single Python code block and no explanation.

Write a Python function `compress_spaces(s)` that replaces every run of space characters in s with a single space and removes leading and trailing spaces. Use only the Python standard library. Respond with the complete function in a single Python code block and no explanation.

Write a Python function `nth_prime(n)` that returns the n-th prime number, counting from nth_prime(1) == 2. Use only the Python standard library. Respond with the complete function in a single Python code block and no explanation.

Write a Python function `hamming_distance(a, b)` that returns the number of positions at which two equal-length strings differ. Use only the Python standard library. Respond with the complete function in a single Python code block and no explanation.

Write a Python function `is_power_of_two(n)` that returns True if the integer n is a positive power of two (1, 2, 4, ...) and False otherwise. Use only the Python standard library. Respond with the complete function in a single Python code block and no explanation.

Write a Python function `collatz_steps(n)` that returns how many steps the Collatz process takes to reach 1 from the positive integer n (halve even numbers, map odd n to 3n+1). Use only the Python standard library. Respond with the complete function in a single Python code block and no explanation.

Write a Python function `invert_dict(d)` that returns a new dictionary with keys and values swapped (all values are distinct strings). Use only the Python standard library. Respond with the complete function in a single Python code block and no explanation.
